newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Telecom's Dean hopes for 97/98 rebound.
newsitem.headline: NZ Telecom's Dean hopes for 97/98 rebound.

text.p: The chief executive of New Zealand's largest company Telecom Corp said on Wednesday he would be disappointed if revenue growth in 1997/98 was not a "a decent rate".

Roderick Deane made the comment to reporters after Telecom announced a fall in its 1996/97 net profits to NZ$518.4 million, alongside an increase in revenue and a 3.2 percent rise in net earnings before one-off items.
Deane rejected suggestions that the company's growth cycle had peaked.
"No," he said when asked if the growth phase had ended. He added that revenues were growing pleasingly despite the slowdown in the New Zealand economy.
"The revenue targets that our people have for both this year and succeeding years are demanding and we expect people to meet them," he said.
Deane added he believed the challenge for the company was to contain costs as volumes grew but prices fell. Strong volume growth had been driving up costs.
He said major shareholder Bell Atlantic was providing help in advising on cost containment.
"We are refocussing on costs. That doesn't mean to say we won't continue to be obsessed with revenues.
"We would be very disappointed if we did not continue to grow our revenues at a decent rate," he said, adding the company would not give any forecasts.
